newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Resources weigh on Australia stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Resources weigh on Australia stocks at close.

text.p: *Stocks slipped further in late trade, hit by fragile metals prices and weaker industrial shares. Turnover 290.50 million, value A$711.67 million, 981 stocks traded, 322 steady, 252 up, 407 down.
The Australian share market slipped further in late trade on Wednesday, hit by continuing fragile metal prices and weaker industrial shares, which had been holding their ground until today.

At 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 19.30 point lower at 2235.10. The September share price index fell 29 points to 2,233 and slipped to a 2.1 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market had been weighted down by warrant related trading in market bellwether BHP, as the warrant came close to expiry, and a generally weaker resource sector.

"The resources are looking quite delicate, while the industrials started to come back a bit today. So in all it's been another poor day and it doesn't look like it's going to get much better for the rest of the week," one Sydney-based dealer said.
The broker said the smaller than expected rise in Australian imports for August had a slight negative effect on the market.

"Those figures were seen as a bit soft, which doesn't help the market. I think we must be running out of good news," he said. Economists said the poor import figures suggest that a interest rate cut remains on the agenda before the end of 1996.

Market action centered on ex-dividend trading in paper group Amcor, options related trading in television broadcaster Seven Network and in casino operator Crown Ltd, after billionaire Kerry Packer sold down his Crown stake on Tuesday.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of five to three.
The largest falls were in the resource sectors, while most of the major industrial sectors were also weaker.

In other markets, Australian bond yields ended only modestly higher as the market rowed back from an initial U.S. led spike after it saw more favourable data to suggest that a local rate cut could be on the cards before the year end.

The Australian dollar slowly lost altitude through a bumpy session as a single large sell order caught the market long and punctured an early rally. At 5.35 p.m. (0735 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$.7880/85.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade picked up after a quiet day on Tuesday. Total options traded 57,814 (38,613) covering 278 issues. Turnover in September SPI contracts totalled 9,245.
